rd.heading: Research & Development Expenses (R&D Expenses)
rd.text: R&D expenses for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 increased 5,198.4% and 719.1%, respectively, compared with the corresponding periods in 2025. The increase in research and development expense was primarily attributable to a more deliberate allocation of engineering labor and other development costs to research and development activities. The increase was primarily related to engineering labor at LWA associated with the redesign of certain systems and related technical re-certification efforts, as well as other product development activities across the Company.

ga.heading: Selling, General & Administrative Expenses
ga.text:
SG&A increased 25.1% and 52.7% for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared with the corresponding periods in 2025. The increase in SG&A expense was primarily attributable to higher payroll, professional fees and advertising expense. For the nine-month period, the increase also reflects higher rent and occupancy costs and other operating expenses. SG&A expenses were comprised of the following:

Payroll, selling and administrative expense increased 22.4% and 10.7% for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared with the corresponding periods in 2025. The increase in payroll expense reflects additional personnel hired during 2026 and higher staffing costs associated with increased operating activity.

Non-cash stock compensation expense increased 83.3% and 27.8% for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared with the corresponding periods in 2025. The increase in non-cash stock compensation expense reflects additional equity compensation recognized for directors and employees during 2026.

Professional fees increased 405.5% and 71.1% for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared with the corresponding periods in 2025. The increase in professional fees was primarily attributable to higher audit, legal, consulting and other professional fees.

nonint.text: Operating expenses consist of selling, general and administrative (“SG&A”) expenses and research and development costs and are reported on a consolidated basis for our operating segments. Total operating expenses increased 27.0% and 53.6% for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared with the corresponding periods in 2025. R&D expenses increased 5,198.4% and 719.1% for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared with the corresponding periods in 2025.

nonop.heading: Other Income/Expense
nonop.text: For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, other income was $377,576 and $1,228,604, respectively, compared with $114,315 for each of the corresponding periods in 2025. Interest expense was $28,606 and $146,228 for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared with $55,587 and $53,804 for the corresponding periods in 2025. The increase in other income was primarily attributable to the Internal Revenue Service’s Employee Retention Credit related income, the write-off and settlement of certain historical liabilities, prior-period accounting corrections and other adjustments identified through the Company’s ongoing reconciliation and financial reporting processes, as well as other refunds and non-operating items. Other income during the third quarter also included gains associated with the disposition of certain assets and additional adjustments resulting from the reconciliation of historical account balances. Several of these items are non-recurring and we believe are not indicative of the Company’s ongoing operating performance.

ocf.text: Net cash provided by operating activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $711,316. Net cash provided by operating activities primarily reflects net income for the period, adjusted for non-cash items and changes in operating assets and liabilities. Cash generated from earnings and increases in accounts payable and accrued liabilities was partially offset by increased investment in inventory, higher accounts receivable and prepaid expenses, and cash payments associated with operating leases.

wc.text: Total current assets increased to $4,552,209 at September 30, 2026 from $3,040,113 at December 31, 2025, while total current liabilities increased to $2,690,775 from $2,461,040. Working capital increased to $1,861,433 from $579,073. The increase in current assets was primarily attributable to increases in cash, inventory, accounts receivable, and prepaid expenses and other current assets. The increase in current liabilities was primarily attributable to higher accounts payable and accrued liabilities and operating lease liabilities, partially offset by reductions in current debt balances. As a result, working capital increased significantly from December 31, 2025.

capex.text: Net cash used in investing activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $29,022. Net cash used in investing activities was primarily attributable to purchases of property and equipment. The acquisition of Sunrise Paddleboards was principally a non-cash transaction and therefore did not materially affect investing cash flows during the period.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

Our principal sources of liquidity are sales of equity and debt securities.

Our success mainly depends on our ability to use and develop our technology and product designs without infringing upon the intellectual property rights of third parties.
